note: Adapted from the species description of Tauritermes bandeirai by Scheffrahn & Vasconcellos (2020), originally in English; the last row of the soldier measurement table records the antennal segment count as 10.58, clearly a typographical error, and is not included; figure numbers and distribution records are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier has conspicuous, stout frontal horns and rounded dorsal horns, which distinguish it from the other three species: in T. triceromegas the dorsal and frontal horns are more angular but much smaller, scarcely rising above the frontal surface in oblique view; in T. vitulus the dorsal horns are similar to those of this species but the frontal horns are absent; in T. taurocephalus the dorsal horns are higher and more angular, and the frontal horns are also absent. In the soldier of this species the frontal surface and the horns are more rugose, the basal swelling of the mandibles is broader and more angular, and antennal segment 3 is more clavate. The shape of the postmentum resembles only that of T. taurocephalus; in T. triceromegas the posterior part of the postmentum is elongate, and in T. vitulus the posterior part is widened. The alate has no distinctive features in the head and pronotum apart from the relatively very large ocelli and the smaller compound eyes; in the fore wing the media is sclerotized at the distal third and closely appressed to the radial sector.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule in dorsal view deep chestnut brown from the postclypeus to the antennal carinae, becoming orange toward the vertex; the head capsule narrows toward the antennal carinae, which are rugose and visible in dorsal view. Frontal carina V-shaped, deeply cleft in the middle. Vertex and cheeks with about ten or more fine setae. Eye spot transparent, narrowly oval. In lateral view the dorsal horns form rounded, nearly right-angled arches; frontal horns projecting above the mandibular bases; genal horns slightly behind the frontal horns and in front of the dorsal horns. Pronotum shield-shaped, wider than the head; anterior margin rugose, deeply concave in the middle, the anterior lobes rounded. In oblique view the dorsal and frontal horns clearly rise above the frontal surface, the horns and frontal surface coarsely rugose. Postclypeus long, nearly a symmetrical hexagon. Antennal segment 3 slightly clavate, the relative lengths of the segments 2<3>4=5. Mandibles about two-fifths as long as the head capsule; basal swelling stout and rugose, its outer margin parallel. Outer margin of the mandible nearly straight in dorsal view, turning at a right angle at one-fifth from the apex; apical tooth stout, marginal tooth weak; in lateral view the mandible evenly curved about 15°. Measurements: head length (to the mandibular apex) 1.95–2.25 mm; head length (to the postclypeus) 1.30–1.50 mm; head width 0.95–1.20 mm; span across the antennal carinae 0.98–1.18 mm; span across the dorsal horns 0.72–0.95 mm; span across the frontal horns 0.82–0.98 mm; pronotum width 0.98–1.19 mm, length 0.70–0.93 mm; postmentum maximum width 0.33–0.40 mm, minimum width 0.18–0.26 mm, median width 0.50–0.68 mm; head height (excluding postmentum) 0.77–0.96 mm.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule and pronotum pale brown. Compound eyes obtusely triangular; ocelli slightly paler than the vertex, very large, roundly oval, nearly touching the ocular margin. Vertex with about ten or more short setae. Pronotum about as wide as the head; anterior margin slightly concave in the middle; several tens of setae in the middle, about ten or more on each lateral margin. Antennae 15-segmented, the relative lengths of the basal segments 1>2<3>4. In the fore wing the subcosta merges with the costa at about one-eighth of the wing length from the wing suture; the radius merges with the costa at about one-third of the wing length; the radial sector has about 4 anterior branches; the media is slightly sclerotized at the distal third and close to the radial sector; the wing membrane and the first 4–5 branches of the cubitus are pale, concolorous with the distal radial sector and media. Arolium present. Measurements: head width excluding the compound eyes 0.63–0.88 mm (female), 0.79–0.86 mm (male); including the compound eyes 0.70–1.04 mm (female), 0.91–0.98 mm (male); pronotum width 0.90–1.08 mm (female), 0.83–0.90 mm (male); compound eye diameter 0.30–0.35 mm (female), 0.26–0.30 mm (male); body length 4.56–6.32 mm (female), 4.88–5.36 mm (male).
